synopsis: Hexagon supplies the Vehicle Intervention System for surface-mining haulage rather than acting as a machine OEM; the corpus groups its off-road braking offerings with systems limited by reverse-only operation, low speed or tag dependence [f1661, f1239]. Hexagon announced on 25 March 2026 that its current-generation system had passed University of Pretoria TRL4 verification before integrated site testing, but the release supplied no performance numbers; an earlier generation reportedly accumulated more than 10,000 working-mine test hours [f1350, f6373, f1353]. No independent performance test was found, and the vendor-reported move to 4D radar in 2024 does not independently establish radar-only adverse-environment validation or prove sensor diversity's effectiveness [f1242, f1747, f1748, f1749]. A 2026 review identifies Hexagon digital-twin platforms as operational in some tier-1 mines, but updating at operational rather than perception timescales [f3827, f3828]. Cadence acquired Hexagon's Design & Engineering business, including VTD, on 23 February 2026 for about USD 3.1 billion; the glossary records both VTD and VTDx moving to Cadence, while their documented evidence remains on-road-only and public prices were not found [f8330, f15891, f15890]. Hexagon separately spun off Octave in May 2026 [f8331, f8884].
